documents.title: Generative AI Syllabus Statements
tiers: Open Use: Permitted in this Course with Attribution
Moderate Use: Permitted when Assigned in this Course with Attribution
Closed: Not Permitted in this Course
documents.summary: The teaching center supplies three ready-to-use syllabus statements, open, moderate and closed, that faculty can adopt or adapt. Open and moderate statements require disclosure with a sample acknowledgment; the closed statement bans AI and calls its use misconduct. A short data-privacy caution applies to all.
documents.stance_why: The page offers three syllabus statements (Open "Permitted in this Course with Attribution", Moderate "Permitted when Assigned", Closed "Not Permitted") for faculty to choose from and recommends instructors outline expectations, so the document sets no single stance and delegates by tiers.

units.why: The page recommends that faculty state AI expectations in their syllabi: "We recommend clearly outlining when and how students should use these tools". It is a recommendation to instructors about communicating rules, so P09 with modality should.

documents.title: Faculty Handbook - AI in Higher Education (introduces Policy 220)
documents.summary: A Faculty Handbook page that introduces Policy 220 (required by Tennessee law, effective July 1, 2025) and lists AI resources: the AI Task Force, the revised academic-integrity policy, syllabus statements and the AI Academy. It contains little rule text of its own.
documents.stance_why: The page introduces Policy 220 and points to syllabus statements and resources but states no use rule itself ("Policy 220 ... is Tennessee Tech's authoritative resource and takes precedence"), so it sets no stance.

units.why: "Tennessee Tech is committed to ensuring its students, faculty, and staff stay up-to-date and are equipped with the knowledge and resources" states an institution-level commitment and purpose, so P56 (framework/preamble).
units.anchor: Tennessee Tech is committed to ensuring its students, faculty, and staff stay up-to-date
units.frag_start: As generative AI continues to evolve

units.why: The page cites state law: institutions "must adopt a policy" on AI use by students, faculty and staff by July 1, 2025. This is a legal mandate behind Policy 220, so P77 (comply with existing law).
units.anchor: institutions must adopt a policy
units.frag_start: Pursuant to T.C.A. 49-8-203(a); T.C.A.

units.why: "Policy 220 ... is Tennessee Tech's authoritative resource and takes precedence over any information provided on this website" sets the policy's standing; nearest type is P56 (institution framework), but precedence is not captured.
